title: TwoSidedClaim.compose() floor-vs-threshold check bypassed by direct construction
description: soundness.py TwoSidedClaim is frozen dataclass with all validation in the compose() classmethod (checks witness.violation_floor() vs threshold before allowing miss_bound>0). No __post_init__. Confirmed empirically: TwoSidedClaim(false_alarm_bound=0.05, miss_bound=0.9, threshold=1.0, violation_floor=0.5, justification='fake') constructs cleanly even though compose() would have raised SoundnessNotEstablished for the same threshold/floor/miss combination. Unlike VerifiedDiscrepancyWitness, ALL fields compose()'s safety check needs (threshold, violation_floor, miss_bound) ARE stored fields -- so this can and should be re-validated in __post_init__, not just gated by a sentinel.
notes: Fixed: added TwoSidedClaim.__post_init__ that re-runs compose()'s floor-vs-threshold check using the stored fields (threshold, violation_floor, miss_bound), raising SoundnessNotEstablished on the same condition compose() checks. Test: test_certabstain.py::test_two_sided_claim_direct_construction_reruns_composes_check (direct-construction bypass + a passing combination still constructs). uv run --group dev pytest -q test_certabstain.py -k 'sound or claim or margin or empirical' -> 6 passed.
close_reason: Fixed via __post_init__ re-validation; test added and passing

title: witness2.py bind()/build() invariants bypassed by direct dataclass construction
description: VerifiedDiscrepancyWitness.bind() checks net weight-hash + reference_id match; PredictiveTubeWitness.build() checks horizon requirements. Both are @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) with NO __post_init__, so calling the raw constructor (VerifiedDiscrepancyWitness(certificate=.., inner=..)) skips every check -- confirmed empirically: constructed a witness with a fake certificate whose matches_network() returns False, bypassing spec A4/A1 entirely; constructed PredictiveTubeWitness with tube.horizon=1 < required_horizon=5 and got a justification string that falsely claims 'declared requirement 5, met'. For PredictiveTubeWitness, all fields the horizon check needs (tube, required_horizon) are stored fields, so __post_init__ can re-validate directly. For VerifiedDiscrepancyWitness, the check needs 'net' and 'reference_id' args that are NOT stored fields, so re-validation in __post_init__ is impossible -- needs a sentinel-token construction guard (same idiom as the existing _RequireRequested/_REQUIRE_REQUESTED sentinel already in this file) to make direct construction unreachable instead.
notes:
Fixed both dataclasses in witness2.py.
PredictiveTubeWitness: moved build()'s horizon-requirement validation into __post_init__ (all inputs -- tube, required_horizon -- are stored fields), so build() now just resolves the _REQUIRE_REQUESTED sentinel and lets __post_init__ enforce the check on every construction path, direct or via build(). Test: test_witness2.py::test_direct_construction_bypassing_build_still_enforces_horizon.
VerifiedDiscrepancyWitness: bind()'s checks need net/reference_id, which are not stored fields, so __post_init__ cannot re-derive them. Added a sentinel-token guard (_BindToken/_BIND_TOKEN, unexported, same idiom as the file's existing _RequireRequested/_REQUIRE_REQUESTED) as an extra frozen-dataclass field defaulting to None; __post_init__ raises TypeError unless the token is the one only bind() supplies. Test: test_witness2.py::test_direct_construction_bypassing_bind_is_rejected.
Grepped repo for other direct constructions of either class outside witness2.py/tests -- none found. uv run --group dev pytest -q test_witness2.py -> 21 passed.
close_reason: Fixed both classes; tests added and passing

title: Interval.lo/.hi (and siblings) are caller-revocable via setflags
description: Interval.__init__ calls lo_arr.setflags(write=False) on an array it owns. Because the array OWNS its data, numpy permits the owner to call setflags(write=True) again at any time -- confirmed empirically: iv.lo.setflags(write=True); iv.lo[0]=999 mutates a 'frozen' Interval, including into an inverted lo>hi state the constructor would have rejected. Same root-cause pattern (setflags(write=False) on an owned array) recurs in nnbound.py MLP.__post_init__ (W,b) and discrepancy.py EpsilonCertificate.__post_init__ (eps, domain_lo/hi, cover_lo/hi, empirical_floor) -- confirmed both are equally revocable. Fix: freeze via np.frombuffer(arr.tobytes()) instead of setflags -- bytes are immutable at the C buffer level so setflags(write=True) permanently fails (verified). Apply to all three sites.
notes: Fixed: added interval._freeze() helper (round-trip through tobytes() so the array no longer owns its data; numpy then refuses setflags(write=True), confirmed empirically -- raises ValueError 'cannot set WRITEABLE flag to True of this array'). Applied at all 3 confirmed sites: interval.py Interval.__init__ (lo/hi), nnbound.py MLP.__post_init__ (W/b per layer), discrepancy.py EpsilonCertificate.__post_init__ (eps/domain_lo/domain_hi/cover_lo/cover_hi/empirical_floor). Swept whole repo for other setflags call sites -- none remain outside interval.py's own docstring/comments and the new test. Tests added: test_interval.py::test_interval_endpoints_cannot_be_unfrozen_via_setflags, test_nnbound.py::test_mlp_weights_cannot_be_unfrozen_via_setflags, test_discrepancy.py::test_certificate_arrays_cannot_be_unfrozen_via_setflags. All 3 files' suites pass (40 passed).
close_reason: Fixed at all 3 sites (interval.py/nnbound.py/discrepancy.py) via interval._freeze() helper; regression tests added and passing

title: conformal.py calibrators: fit()'s validation bypassed by direct construction
description: SplitConformalCalibrator and MondrianCalibrator are frozen dataclasses whose only validation lives in their fit() classmethods (_check_alpha, sample-size checks). No __post_init__ on either. Confirmed empirically: SplitConformalCalibrator(threshold=-999.0, alpha=5.0, n=-1, order_statistic=999) constructs cleanly, and its coverage_lower property then reports -4.0 and false_alarm_bound reports 5.0 -- nonsense probabilities. Full data-consistency (that threshold really is the order_statistic-th order stat of some real calibration sample) can't be re-derived from stored fields alone (the raw scores aren't kept), but the structural invariants (alpha in (0,1), n>=1, 1<=order_statistic<=n, threshold finite) can and should be checked in __post_init__.
notes:
Fixed both calibrators in conformal.py. SplitConformalCalibrator.__post_init__ now checks the structural invariants fit() also enforces (alpha in (0,1) via _check_alpha, n>=1, order_statistic in [1,n], threshold finite) -- explicitly NOT full data-consistency (that threshold really is the order_statistic-th order stat of some real sample), which can't be re-derived without the raw scores; documented as a deliberate scope limit in the __post_init__ docstring. MondrianCalibrator.__post_init__ checks alpha in (0,1) and that every per-stratum SplitConformalCalibrator's own alpha matches the Mondrian object's alpha (an internal-consistency check fit() always satisfies but a direct constructor could violate); the per-stratum minimum-size check itself needs raw scores and is out of scope for the same reason.
Tests: test_certabstain.py::test_split_conformal_direct_construction_rejects_nonsense_fields, test_mondrian_direct_construction_rejects_inconsistent_alpha.
Grepped repo for other direct constructions outside conformal.py/tests -- none found.
uv run --group dev pytest -q test_certabstain.py -k 'conformal or split or mondrian or calibrat or shift or two_sided or refuses' -> 17 passed.
close_reason: Fixed both calibrators with scoped structural validation; tests added and passing

title: reference.py frozen dataclasses: verify direct-construction claim (audit)
description: Sandbox prompt claims SpringDamper2D/PusherSlider/CircleClearance in reference.py can be constructed directly, skipping 'whatever the blessed factory enforces.' Empirically checked: all three only have __post_init__ (no separate bind()/build() classmethod), and __post_init__ IS part of the dataclass-generated __init__, so it runs on every construction path including direct calls. Confirmed SpringDamper2D(m=-1.0), PusherSlider(c=0.0001), CircleClearance(r=-1.0) all raise ValueError as expected. Conclusion pending write-up: no fix needed here, direct constructor already validates. Document reasoning in handoff.
notes: Confirmed no fix needed: SpringDamper2D/PusherSlider/CircleClearance in reference.py have only __post_init__ (no separate bind()/build()/fit() classmethod), and __post_init__ is part of the dataclass-generated __init__, so it runs on every construction path including direct calls -- there is no bypassable factory here, unlike soundness.py/witness2.py/conformal.py. Verified empirically: SpringDamper2D(m=-1.0), PusherSlider(c=0.0001), CircleClearance(r=-1.0) all raise. Added the one gap found: CircleClearance's refusal path (negative radius, non-finite params) had no test anywhere in the suite -- added test_reference.py::test_reference_dataclasses_have_no_bypassable_factory. PusherSlider/SpringDamper2D refusals were already covered by test_parameter_construction_refusals. uv run --group dev pytest -q test_reference.py -> 10 passed.
close_reason: Audited; no bypass exists; added missing CircleClearance regression test

title: Sibling-path sweep: gate.py/tube.py/nnbound.py/discrepancy.py factory-bypass audit
description: Mandatory sibling-path sweep (sandbox-prompt.md) after fixing the setflags bug (certabstain-136), TwoSidedClaim (certabstain-oot), witness2.py (certabstain-qkf), conformal.py (certabstain-0dq), reference.py (certabstain-quc). Checked remaining frozen dataclasses for the 'validation lives only in a bypassable factory' bug shape: SafetyCertificate/GateDecision in gate.py, TubeResult in tube.py, MLP.random() in nnbound.py, EpsilonCertificate/certify_epsilon() in discrepancy.py.
design:
SafetyCertificate (gate.py): guarantee is cryptographic (HMAC tag from CertificateAuthority._tag(), verified via hmac.compare_digest in CertificateVerifier), not constructor validation -- direct construction with a forged tag still fails verify(). No bypassable-factory shape.
GateDecision (gate.py): plain output carrier, asserts no invariant of its own.
TubeResult (tube.py): only one construction site (propagate_tube() line 255), no separate classmethod factory -- same shape as reference.py (no fix needed there either). The safety-relevant guarantee (horizon requirement) is asserted by its consumer PredictiveTubeWitness, already fixed in witness2.py to re-validate in __post_init__.
MLP.random() (nnbound.py): confirmed it does 'return cls(tuple(ws), activation=activation)' -- goes through the same dataclass __init__/__post_init__ as any other construction path. No separate validation to bypass.
EpsilonCertificate/certify_epsilon() (discrepancy.py): certify_epsilon() enforces CoverTooSmall, TargetNotCertified, and finite-target/finite-min_cover_fraction refusals that are NOT re-derivable from EpsilonCertificate's stored fields alone. But unlike TwoSidedClaim/SplitConformalCalibrator, bypassing these does not produce an unsound certificate: cover_fraction is explicitly documented as diagnostic (not used by contains()/matches_network()/the gate for any safety decision), and a target miss just means the certificate reports a looser eps than requested, not an incorrect one -- eps/cover_lo/cover_hi (the fields consumers actually rely on for soundness) are unaffected by skipping those two checks. __post_init__ already re-validates the one true soundness invariant every construction path needs: eps must be finite. No fix needed; recorded because the reasoning is non-obvious.
acceptance_criteria: Conclusions recorded in a bead (this one) and in sandbox-handoff.md; no source changes needed for these four files beyond what earlier beads already did.
close_reason: Audited all four files; no bypassable-factory bug shape found. Reasoning recorded in issue design field.
